title: Accepted Circuit Encoding and Evaluation
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $R$ be a finite bit string, let $P$ be a finite list of finite bit strings, and let $G$ be a finite bit string. If the run initialized from the context determined by $n$, $R$, and $P$, together with $G$, has a nonempty word that is done, then there is a finite list $gs$ of arithmetic gates on $n$ inputs such that $G$ is the encoding of $gs$, every gate at position $i$ refers only to gates at positions less than $i$, and the run equals the encoding of that context, the word consisting of the single bit $0$, and the list of gate values obtained by evaluating $gs$ modulo $\mathrm{bitsVal}(R)+1$ with input values $i \mapsto \mathrm{bitsVal}(P_i)+1$.
hypotheses_covered: $P$ is a finite list of finite bit strings
the run initialized from the encoded context and $G$ has a nonempty word that is done
